name: Learn basic DJ beatmatching
blurb: Getting two tracks running at the same tempo and phase, by ear. Software will sync for you, but hearing the drift is what makes you a DJ rather than an operator.
gear: Two decks or DJ software with a controller
steps: Learn to count in phrases: four beats to a bar, eight or sixteen bars to a phrase. Almost all dance music is built this way.
Learn to cue: find the first beat of a phrase and set the cue point precisely.
Match tempo by ear using the pitch fader, listening for whether the incoming track is fast or slow relative to the master.
Learn the nudge: touch the jog wheel to correct phase without changing tempo.
Practise holding two tracks in sync for a full minute with the sync button off.
Learn a simple mix in and out over 16 bars, with the EQ swapping the basslines.
tips: Two basslines at once is the single ugliest sound in DJing. Cut the incoming low end until the swap.
Turn sync off while practising. Learning to hear drift is the entire skill.
proof: You hold two tracks beatmatched by ear for a minute and complete a clean transition, sync disabled.
